name: Homeostasis, the nervous system, the brain and the eye

terms.definition: The regulation of the internal conditions of a cell or organism to maintain optimum conditions for function in response to internal and external changes.
terms.examiner: Body temperature, blood glucose and water levels are controlled.

terms.definition: A cell that detects a stimulus (a change in the environment).
A muscle or gland that brings about a response.
An automatic, rapid response that does not involve the conscious part of the brain.
terms.examiner: The reflex arc uses sensory, relay and motor neurones.

terms.definition: The gap between two neurones; a chemical diffuses across it to start an impulse in the next neurone.
terms.examiner: Synapses slow the impulse slightly but let it go only one way.

terms.definition: The part of the brain responsible for memory, language, intelligence and consciousness.
terms.examiner: Separate Biology: cerebellum controls muscle coordination; medulla controls unconscious actions such as heart rate.

terms.definition: Changing the shape of the lens to focus on near or distant objects.
terms.examiner: Near object: ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments slacken, lens becomes thicker.

terms.definition: The part of the brain that monitors and controls body temperature, with receptors sensitive to blood temperature.
terms.examiner: Separate Biology. Too hot: vasodilation and sweating. Too cold: vasoconstriction and shivering.
